items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: I was reading this book by Walter Isaacson, a terrific writer, Einstein: His Life and Universe.

ctx.x: Thank you. I knew I’d mispronounce that but I thought, “Oh that’s interesting she wrote a song about a law firm.” So you know I did some digging and where did the idea to write about subatomic particles come from?

I don’t know where these ideas come from sometimes but I had — I was reading this book by Walter Isaacson, a terrific writer, Einstein: His Life and Universe. And I was thinking of this episode of “Frasier” my ex-husband used to play in the warm-up band for “Frasier” because it was done live. And there was a scene in which Frasier was going on a tropical vacation and his family was there and his latest girlfriend was there, and Frasier is just being a real jerk. He’s complaining about everything. And the…

dollars. So they were just in despair. And then I saw these names of the elementary particles and I thought it was “mayson” too but I looked it up, Hadron, Meson, Baryon. And I thought well that’s kind of a hooky little — that would make a good hook. Hadron, Meson, Baryon. So I created a little story about a class of people who are in despair and they’re wondering what’s at the bottom of it all and the physicist in the story is a woman and she goes back and she’s with her husband. And you know it’s just — writing…
